text.content:
There must be an active scene to use the notebook app.

  • Open it with the notebook icon in the left control bar, directly below "Journal Notes". The keybinding CTRL+J works as well.

  • If the scene has no notebook yet, the app shows a button that creates one and links it to the scene.

  • To use an existing notebook instead, drag'n'drop the notebook item onto the app.

  • You don't need to edit the notebook item directly. Use the notebook app.

  • Drag'n'drop actors directly onto the notebook app to add them.

The notebook stores its data scene based. So, if you switch the scene, it could display another notebook item if the other scene got already configured.

Play a little bit around with the notebook app. It's easy and intuitive.

If you want to place a macro in your macro bar, create a macro of type script with the following code:

NotebookApp.getInstance().render(true, { focus: true })

Two different kinds of markup are used, depending on the field.

Checklist entries

Entries of a checklist item are plain text and support bbCode:

  • [b]bold[/b]

  • [i]italic[/i]

  • [u]underline[/u]

  • [s]strikethrough[/s]

  • [br] line break

  • [list]item 1[br]item 2[br]item 3[/list]

Descriptions

The description and the move description of an item are rich text fields. Use the editor — HTML tags belong here, bbCode does not.

Roll outcomes

Mark a roll outcome with [ON …] at the start of a line. It is rendered as a coloured badge in front of the text, and it works in checklist entries as well as in the description and move description of a move.

  • [ON 12+] you also find a Clue; the Keeper will describe it.

  • [ON 10+] the magic works without further cost: choose your effect.

  • [ON 7-9] the magic works imperfectly: choose your effect and a complication.

  • [ON 6-] the Keeper reacts.

  • [ON hit] you find a Clue. The Keeper will tell you what it is.

  • [ON miss] you glimpse a terrible fate awaiting one of your fellow Hunters.

Number ranges are shown exactly as written. hit and miss are translated through the language file, so a translation never has to touch the tag itself — only the text around it. Any other token still gets a badge, just without a colour, which makes a typo visible instead of silently dropping the marker.

For older content the English wording "On a 10+, …" is still recognised, but new and translated text should use the tag.

The Playbooks compendium holds ready-made character sheets, sorted into one folder per game:

  • The Between — The American, The Explorer, The Factotum, The Mother, The Orphan, The Undeniable, The Vessel

  • Public Access — Latchkey

  • Brindlewood Bay — Murder Maven

Drag a playbook into the actors directory and the whole sheet comes with it: moves, checklists, abilities and the XP track of that game.

Choosing moves

Every move of a playbook is on the sheet from the start. The move you begin with is active, the optional ones are greyed out. Tick the checkbox in the header of a move card to activate the one you picked — and untick it again if you change your mind. Nothing is hidden, so you never have to switch to edit mode for this.

More moves

The Items compendium carries the move collections that are chosen from rather than shipped with a playbook, for example "Public Access Latchkey Moves" and the Maven Moves of Brindlewood Bay. Drag one onto a character sheet to add it.
